evidence_for: Main mechanism is supported by support-repair audit; MuSiQue limitation is now quantified; negative pilots are clean and useful for limitations.
evidence_against: Does not solve the full MuSiQue gap; needs careful framing so limitations do not look like hidden method failure.
required_next_evidence: No more experiments required before drafting; only paper tables/figures need packaging.

evidence_for: Could test whether dependency-bound control becomes useful when slot queries are LLM-reformulated instead of lexical.
evidence_against: D-BIR-det is negative; earlier chain-walking LLM probe was weak; risk of continuing MuSiQue-specific sunk-cost exploration.
required_next_evidence: Within <=3 days, compare D-BIR-LLM against LLM-reformulate-independent-demand on the same slices. Continue only if D-BIR wins by >=10pp Exp@50 and Final New@5 >=15-20%.
recommendation: Do only if the user explicitly wants one last kill-switch probe.

evidence_for: Pool-absent recovery is strongest in the D-BIR pilot: 28.0% at @100.
evidence_against: Novelty is weak because this is close to query decomposition / decompose-then-retrieve / LevelRAG-style expansion.
required_next_evidence: Literature review must identify a clear non-overlapping claim before implementation.
recommendation: Do not start engineering before novelty check.

evidence_for: Could overcome train-free lexical/LLM heuristic ceilings.
evidence_against: Large engineering cost; overlaps CoRAG-style trained retrieval; unclear differentiation.
required_next_evidence: Need a new method claim and training/eval budget.
recommendation: Do not pursue as a DBEC sequel.

evidence_for: The diagnostics form a strong empirical story about fixed-pool multi-hop ceilings and candidate-generation bottlenecks.
evidence_against: May be less attractive as a standalone method paper; needs broader benchmarks and reviewer-facing framing.
required_next_evidence: Broaden beyond MuSiQue and compare failure mechanisms across methods/datasets.
recommendation: Consider only after DBEC draft is stable.

evidence_for: Strict fixed-pool listwise selection reached New@5 26.7% query-primary and 25.0% all-title, clearly above chain-walking 10.5%. The full1000 RankGPT-style selector confirms missing-slice New@5 20.8-25.0%.
evidence_against: RankGPT-style selector is weaker than DBEC/SetR on overall Support R@5 and Complete@5 across 2Wiki, HotpotQA, and MuSiQue; cost is high because the LLM reads pool100; reader F1 conversion is unknown.
required_next_evidence: Run a small reader evaluation using the best listwise-selected top5 on the MuSiQue slice only if DBEC paper needs a stronger limitation/upper-bound analysis.
recommendation: Optional, not a second-paper direction by itself.

evidence_for: A full reader matrix could answer whether RankGPT-style selector rows translate into QA F1.
evidence_against: Selector-only support metrics already show RankGPT-style no-thinking listwise selection is not an overall DBEC/SetR replacement; broad reader runs would be expensive and unlikely to change the first-paper claim.
required_next_evidence: If demanded by reviewers or draft needs, run only the best listwise selector on MuSiQue first, not all variants across all datasets.

evidence_for: Avoids chasing a dataset-specific failure mode after multiple negative pilots.
evidence_against: Wastes some existing infrastructure and delays output from current line.
required_next_evidence: One-week literature/problem audit to choose a new problem.
recommendation: Healthy option after DBEC paper writing reaches a complete draft.
